title: New study links the fatigue of depression to overworked cellular power plant
author: Petrova, Karina
summary: A study in Translational Psychiatry reveals that depressed individuals display elevated ATP production at baseline while lacking capacity to increase output under stress. Mitochondria appear pushed near limits, creating a system in compensatory overdrive. Cells expend extraordinary effort maintaining ordinary functioning, leaving no reserve for additional demands. This metabolic paradox mirrors depression's psychological experience: constant effort yields little progress. The findings suggest depression involves energy dysregulation at the cellular level, reshaping how the body sustains motivation and vitality.
points: Depressed participants show elevated ATP production at baseline yet cannot increase output when stressed—a metabolic paradox.
Mitochondria in depressed individuals appear pushed near limits during rest, leaving no metabolic reserves for additional demands.
Cells expend extraordinary effort simply maintaining ordinary functioning, mirroring the psychological experience of depression itself.
The metabolic dysfunction suggests depression involves energy dysregulation, not merely emotional disturbance.
This metabolic fatigue operates at the cellular level, reshaping the body's capacity to sustain motivation, cognition, and vitality.
